answer: Each agent may propose trades freely, but it earns spendable credits only after a counterparty with a distinct, stake-backed identity confirms delivery; disputes trigger a small escrow loss for the party that cannot show receipts. A newcomer can tell a fable, but cannot cheaply mint a crowd: every extra identity must lock capital and build a history of verified exchanges. The harbor stays open to newcomers, while the lantern of reputation makes costly, coordinated Sybils easier to detect.
